sourcePieces.description: Upper example: tall rounded rectangular upright metal case, top lid shown in perspective, front and left side visible, seams at top and bottom.
Exactly two separate bent upright metal lugs above the lid, each with an eye/hole and a dark insulating base. The two terminals are not joined.
Exactly two dark mounting feet below the large case; the left foot has a visible mounting hole.

Front printed manufacturer/type/rating panel including a central small emblem, large Cyrillic-like marks and smaller lines. Exact characters and numeric values are not reliably legible at this opening; do not invent readings.
Lower separate example: short cylindrical paper-capacitor case at a slight rising-right tilt, visible left circular end and a curved right rim.
One wire emerges from each end of the small cylinder. Left lead extends down-left; right lead extends up-right. No wire joins either lead to the larger case.
Small printed emblem/type/rating markings on the cylindrical sleeve. Exact text is unresolved; preserve a neutral marking region, without Cyrillic or fabricated ratings.

fig-155.structure: Two independent manufactured examples vertically separated, not a circuit. No visible wound cross-section, axes, grid, measurement, polarity, or cutaway.
modernAdditions: English identification labels and neutral marking panels replace culturally specific/unreadable manufacturer print.

An independently identified enlarged winding detail may be added from the exact modern paragraph: two metal-foil conductors separated by insulating paper, tightly rolled. This is edition-text content, not a claim about visible source internals.
Arrangement may be widened for inline readability, retaining two distinct packages and all visible mechanical pieces.

sourcePieces.description: Large dark ribbed knob above the center-left spindle, shallow domed top and scalloped/ribbed lower edge.
Vertical central spindle extends from knob through the upper frame and plate bank to the lower frame.
Upper and lower bearing/collar assemblies around the shaft; additional visible shaft collars near the plate bank.
One repeated bank of closely spaced thin metal plates extending between the left and right frame sides, supported by the frame; many horizontal plate edges are visible.
A second repeated plate bank on the central shaft projects diagonally toward the front-right, overlapping/interleaving with the fixed bank. The overlap is partial, not two isolated capacitor symbols.
Thin clear spaces between successive plate layers. No dielectric slab is present, and the two banks must not electrically touch.
Open upper perimeter support with triangular/diagonal braces linking the side posts and shaft-bearing location; fastening hardware at the corners.
Open lower perimeter support with triangular/diagonal braces and side fasteners, below the plate stack.
Left and right vertical frame posts, each with top and bottom fastening heads/collars.
Separate front-right upright connection/support post with a top screw/head and stacked collars/spacers, extends below the lower frame.

unresolved: Exact hidden plate count and hidden plate contours cannot be established from this oblique overlapping reproduction. No numeric count is supplied by the lesson.

fig-156.structure: One mechanically complete open-frame air-variable capacitor, two interleaving metal banks, knob mechanically coupled by a shaft, top and bottom supports. No circuit wires, scale, numeric settings, or polarity labels.
modernAdditions: Regularized engineering perspective rather than archival shading; visible layers remain thin, repeated and separated.
English labels identify knob, fixed plates, moving plates and air gaps.
A chosen illustrative repetition count must be declared as a modern diagram regularization, never an asserted original plate count.

sourcePieces.description: Left example: tall upright cylindrical can, rounded upper closure and bottom rolled flange; visible metal sleeve and printed rating area.
Tall can has bottom closure, mounting hardware/hexagonal nut, dark terminal assembly and an axial pin/loop projecting down.
Upper-right example: slender cylinder leaning down-right, visible top/end cap and printed sleeve.
Slender cylinder has exactly two axial leads: short upper lead bends up-left; long lower lead bends down then curls left. They are not wired to other examples.
Lower-right example: shorter wider upright cylinder with prominent top cap/rim, printed sleeve and a bottom rolled rim.
Short can has bottom mounting nut/threaded stud assembly and a narrow separate terminal extension downward; multiple thread ridges are visible.

All three sleeves have original manufacturer/type/rating marks. Tall can visibly includes a rating-like line read as 150 microfarads and 200 volts; exact remaining type/date text, and the other two numeric ratings, are unresolved and must not be guessed.

legibleGivenValues.confidence: visual reading of source marking, not a task given or proposed modern rating

fig-157.structure: Exactly three physically separate electrolytic-capacitor package examples: tall left can, slanted slender axial package above right, short stud-mounted can below right. This is NOT an electrolysis experiment or a wired electrolytic apparatus. No internal oxide-film cutaway or polarity symbols are visibly supplied.
modernAdditions: Neutral sleeve marking regions retain the location of source print; no historical manufacturer lettering or fictional rating values.
English labels for axial leads and mounting stud; no invented polarity assignment to source terminals.
No experiment, beaker, power source or generic capacitor icon may replace these three package structures.
